newsitem.title: UK: Jordan tells Netanyahu of concern over tunnel.
newsitem.headline: Jordan tells Netanyahu of concern over tunnel.

text.p: Jordan voiced concern to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday over the opening of a tourist tunnel in Jerusalem near an Islamic holy site.
Israeli spokesman Shai Bazak said Crown Prince Hassan called the Israeli leader in London where Netanyahu was making an official visit.
"Prince Hassan called Prime Minister Netanyahu this morning from Jordan. He wanted to know what the situation was with the tunnel in Jerusalem," Bazak told reporters.
The tunnel, in the heart of the walled Old City of Jerusalem, runs along the western retaining wall of the Jewish Temple Mount, now the site of al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine.
"The prime minister made it clear to him that the tunnel does not go under the Temple Mount. It won't collapse the Temple Mount. It is an incredible historic project," Bazak said.
The spokesman said Netanyahu told Prince Hassan the tunnel would benefit all residents of the walled Old City, Arabs and Jews alike, and Prince Hassan responded that Israel should make this known.
Israeli Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani said in Jerusalem on Wednesday the tunnel would help the Palestinian economy by drawing tourists and pilgrims to the Old City Arab markets.
